head_drift_note: every rung's block number is head_at_measurement minus its label, so a rung probed late in the run is deeper than its label by up to this drift. At the state bracket the rungs are 2,000 blocks apart, so a drift of this size is a real part of the bracket's width and is not corrected for here.
method: one eth_getBalance of the zero address at (head - N) for each N in the state ladder; one eth_getLogs over a small span at (head - N) for each N in the log ladder, escalated to a narrower span and a longer timeout if it does not answer. A timeout is recorded as a timeout, a span refusal as a span refusal, and neither as an absence. The log queries carry no address filter, so their cost grows with how busy the chain was

block_time.note: the mean of the spans above, which is only usable as a unit because they agree; if spans_agree_within_5pct is false, no single block time describes this chain over this window and a conversion to hours should not be made from it

logs_query_span_cap_evidence: query spans 85470412 blocks (0 to 85470411), but only 10000000 are allowed for this request; narrow the block range
logs_query_row_cap_evidence: logs matched by query exceeds limit of 10000
query_limits_note: two separate limits, measured separately because the first version of this probe hit whichever came first and reported one number: a cap on how many blocks one query may span, and a cap on how many rows one query may match. Neither is a statement about retention.
unresolved_note: a rung here never got an answer from the chain -- a rate limit that survived the backoff, or an error this file does not recognise. It is excluded from every bracket and every claim below. The first run of this ladder filed rate limits as errors and the brackets were computed over them, which made our own request rate look like the chain's retention.
state_retention_prior_measurement: PREREG-oneside-depth-2026-09-25-addendum-4.md records 3,100-5,900 blocks, measured 2026-09-11 to 09-15. This ladder is spaced to be comparable with that rather than coarser than it. State pruning is a node's housekeeping schedule, so the two brackets differing is not by itself an error in either; what would be an error is letting a coarser ladder read as a correction.
state_retention_bracket_note: state retention lies between state_served_at_deepest_blocks_back and state_pruned_at_shallowest_blocks_back. Either bound may be null: null for the served bound means even the shallowest rung was already pruned and this ladder brackets nothing from below, which is what the first version of this probe did without saying so.
logs_claim_note: logs_proven_at_deepest_blocks_back is the deepest rung that came back with at least one row: the node had those logs at that depth, and it is the only positive retention claim in this file. logs_answered_at_deepest_blocks_back counts a query that returned without error even if it returned nothing, and is NOT evidence of retention -- a node that has dropped its log index can answer empty rather than erroring. A rung in logs_refused hit a timeout or a span limit after escalation; both are limits on the query and neither is a statement about retention. An earlier artifact reported the deepest answered rung under a name that read as a boundary, and the rung below it had merely timed out on an unfiltered query; an address-filtered query at a comparable depth answers immediately.
note: state and events are pruned on different schedules on this endpoint, so a retention claim has to name which of the two it is about. Where events are served, realised execution is publicly recheckable; where state is not, a counterfactual figure at a past block can only be rechecked against an archive kept at the time, which is why this project archives its reads.
